coordinates.note: REVIEW REQUIRED (A17), after real effort: no CERN geodetic-survey, metrology paper or official ALICE/CERN page giving WGS84 coordinates for the underground ALICE (UX25) cavern was found this session. Checked: the ALICE detector paper (2008 JINST 3 S08002, chapters 1-2, which give the location in prose - 'Point 2 of the LHC accelerator tunnel in the commune of St. Genis-Pouilly, France' - and depths, but no lat/lon), alice.cern, home.cern's ALICE page, the ALICE Collaboration's own site (alice-collaboration.web.cern.ch), and the ITS2/TPC upgrade TDR abstracts. None states a coordinate. The numeric value is re-fetched this session (2026-09-17) from the same OpenStreetMap/Nominatim query already recorded as src:lep-point-2-osm-nominatim (reused per ID_REGISTRY/worklog instructions rather than duplicated) for the surface-area feature named 'CERN - Point 2 (Alice)'. Per A17, a geocoder source may only back a campus/headquarters kind coordinate, so this is recorded as kind 'campus', not 'detector' - it should be read as 'the general area this marker names', not a surveyed cavern location. precision_m is widened to 300 m accordingly. This is the same physical LHC point as site:cern-lep-point-2-l3 (owned by historic-cern, the LEP-era L3 record); this is a separate, current-era record for ALICE, not a duplicate (Point 2 hosted L3 during LEP and now hosts ALICE, which reuses the L3 solenoid magnet in place - src:colliders-lhc-alice-detector-jinst-2008).

depth.note: The ALICE detector paper's own figure for the UX25 cavern floor depth. home.cern separately states ALICE 'sits in a vast cavern 56 m below ground' (src:lep-cern-alice-experiment-page); the two are not necessarily in conflict (52 m to the cavern floor vs. a ~56 m figure that may describe the average depth of the detector volume or overburden-plus-cavern-height), but no fetched source reconciles them explicitly, so both are recorded: this field uses the detector paper's cavern-floor figure since it is the collaboration's own technical publication (rank 5 vs rank 2).
depth.quote: The beam line is situated 44 m underground as shown in figure 2.1. The floor of the UX25 cavern is 52 m underground and there is 28 m of overburden above the detector.

depth_rock.quote: there is 28 m of overburden above the detector

name: LHC Point 2 (ALICE cavern)
notes: Coordinate kind is 'campus' rather than 'detector'/'underground_lab' because the only coordinate source available in this session is an OpenStreetMap/Nominatim geocoder lookup, and A17 restricts geocoder-backed coordinates to campus/headquarters kind. See coordinates.note for the full account of sources checked.

This is a separate record from site:cern-lep-point-2-l3 (owned by historic-cern), which documents the same physical LHC point during the earlier LEP/L3 era. The two coexist deliberately per the Wave 3 brief: same point, different eras, cross-referenced in prose rather than merged.

detector:alice's placements[] cites this site with role 'main' despite the campus-kind coordinate, following the same pattern used at site:cern-point-1-atlas (an uncertain/approximate coordinate that is still the best available point for the marker).

summary.plain: The underground cavern at Point 2 of the Large Hadron Collider, near the French village of St Genis-Pouilly, where the ALICE experiment records lead-ion and proton collisions. The cavern previously housed the L3 experiment during CERN's earlier LEP collider.
summary.technical: LHC interaction point 2, in the commune of St. Genis-Pouilly (Ain, France): the UX25 experimental cavern, whose floor is 52 m underground with 28 m of rock overburden, houses the ALICE detector inside the L3 solenoid magnet reused from LEP.
